title: Table Inheritance: Mechanics & Trade-offs
description: Understand object-relational table inheritance (INHERITS), polymorphic querying, and why modern schemas prefer declarative partitioning.

data.text: Reflecting its object-relational origins, PostgreSQL supports **Table Inheritance** (`CREATE TABLE ... INHERITS`). A child table inherits all columns and check constraints from its parent table.

data.title: Table Inheritance Example
data.content: Querying parent returns rows from both parent and child.

data.title: Inheritance vs Declarative Partitioning
data.text: Before PostgreSQL 10, table inheritance was used to implement manual partitioning. Modern PostgreSQL schemas should always use declarative partitioning (`PARTITION BY`) instead of `INHERITS` because `INHERITS` does not enforce global uniqueness across parent and child tables.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Child tables inherit columns and constraints from parents.
Use `SELECT * FROM ONLY parent` to exclude child tables.
Use declarative partitioning instead of inheritance for partitioning large datasets.
